pagerbot: PAGE to #incidents — authz anomaly detected: 6xx token-exchange failures + 45 outbound S3 puts from svcacct `svc-ci-runner-23` in last 3m. Severity: P1.

anna-oncall: On it. I'm taking primary. @michael-sre you available?

michael-sre: here, looking. seeing a cluster of requests from 3 IPs in APAC hitting `/v1/token/exchange`. UA looks like `gitlab-runner/14.3` and `curl/7.82`.

jamal-ops: noticing retries with `x-retry-id` headers. Some PUTs to an external bucket dns name `s3-external-snap.example` — likely misconfigured CI artifact upload.

kevin-sre: any customer-facing errors? I only see internal token-exchange 401/403 spikes. No increase in API 5xx.

anna-oncall: good. michael, can you confirm which service account is being used for the CI runners?

michael-sre: yes — `svc-ci-runner-23` (IAM role `ci-runner`) used by multiple ephemeral runners. Last rotated 18d ago.

elena-security: @anna-oncall escalate to secops. Please create a short evidence bundle (logs + sample requests). Also freeze that service account credentials now.

anna-oncall: doing freeze. Running quick revoke:

```
# revoke active tokens associated with svc-ci-runner-23
rbacctl revoke --service-account svc-ci-runner-23 --all-active
```

kevin-sre: ran revoke, returned 13 sessions revoked. Output: `revoked:13; errors:0`. Pushing immediate WAF rules to block the 3 IP ranges:

```
wafctl block-ip 203.0.113.0/24 --reason "suspicious ci-runner traffic"
wafctl block-ip 198.51.100.0/24
wafctl block-ip 192.0.2.0/25
```

jamal-ops: blocking applied, confirmed on edge. I also added a temporary rule to deny outbound S3 PUTs to unknown hosts from the runner role.

michael-sre: running quick grep to find exposed tokens in staging logs: 
```
# search for obvious token fragments in last 48h of staging logs
logq "svc-ci-runner-23" | jq -r '.message' | grep -E "(token|access|secret)[:=]" | head -n 50
```

michael-sre: found 7 log lines with truncated token fragments in staging only — not prod. Looks like a debugging print from a flaky artifact upload helper.

elena-security: good find. That suggests limited exposure surface (staging only) but we treat as incident. Next steps: 1) rotate keys for svc-ci-runner-23 2) scrub staging logs and re-ingest clean 3) notify legal/PR for potential customer impact if any tokens match active ones.

anna-oncall: executing rotation now.

```
# rotate credentials
rbacctl rotate --service-account svc-ci-runner-23 --generate-new-keys --force
```

kevin-sre: rotation succeeded. New creds pushed to vault path `secret/ci/svc-ci-runner-23`. CI runners instructed to pick up new creds at next job start. Added short TTL to the vault key (4h) while we validate.

jamal-ops: scrub job scheduled. Running retention-delete for the affected staging index and snapshot.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: "Auth Token Leak Triage" — checklist created: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/auth-token-leak. Steps auto-added to incident.

elena-security: start customer-impact review. michael, can you correlate the 7 truncated fragments with any active keys (fuzzy match)? Use `keymatch` tool.

michael-sre: running `keymatch --fuzzy fragments.txt --source vault` now.

michael-sre: result: NO active key match. All matching keys were already rotated or belong to ephemeral staging-only test accounts.

elena-security: OK that's good. Still treat as P1 because of attempted exfil. We'll escalate to SecOps for forensic timeline and retention.

anna-oncall: I'm posting an incident bridge for customer-impact triage and handoff to secops. Bridge: https://bridge.redwood/2167000001

anna-oncall: provisional status: containment achieved (revoke + block + rotate + scrub job scheduled). Impact: internal staging tokens exposed only, no customer production tokens found.

jamal-ops: creating follow-up tickets: TASK-4821 rotate any other long-lived runner service accounts, TASK-4822 audit CI runner image that prints debug logs.

elena-security: adding legal and compliance to watch. Please preserve all evidence, do not delete raw logs until SecOps confirms.

kevin-sre: handing off to secops oncall @elena-security for long-term investigation. I'll stay on standby for any rollout fallout.

elena-security: accepted handoff. Next actions: full timeline, IP attribution, coordinate with partner hosting the external bucket, and prepare short customer-facing summary if needed.

anna-oncall: thanks team. I'll turn off pager for this thread and mark as mitigated for oncall rotation. Leave long-term tasks to secops and ops. :white_check_mark:

pagerbot: NOTE: incident marked "contained" by anna-oncall at 2167000034. Follow-ups: TASK-4821, TASK-4822, SecOps investigation.
